item.title: Hegseth's failed impeachment was a warning to Democrats. Where will they go from here?
item.description:

November 14, 20265:00 AM ET

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., speaks during a news conference on Nov. 4, 2025, on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C.
Tom Brenner/Getty Images
hide caption

Democrats are not in the majority yet, but the first post-election test of their ability to get things done was a failure.
The House was unable to advance an impeachment effort of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Eleven Democrats were no-shows for the vote. Based on the math in this vote: If those 11 had been there and if no more Republicans showed up, the attempt would have gone forward.
Now, for those who want to see Hegseth impeached, it's fair to ask why only one Republican was in favor of it, Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky, who led the effort, especially after an election that saw GOP wipeouts in no small measure because of the Iran war? The GOP still controls the floor, so a Democratic speaker would have been able to leave the vote open longer for the 11 to be able to cast their votes.

item.description:
Health Policy
An organ transplant controversy tests 'the dead donor rule'
November 14, 20265:00 AM ET
Rob Stein
New guidelines are supposed to protect organ donors in a retrieval procedure that keeps blood flowing through livers, kidneys, lungs and hearts. But bioethicists have troubling questions.
Olga Pankova/Getty Images
hide caption

Olga Pankova/Getty Images
The U.S. organ transplant system has approved the first national policy for a controversial procedure used to remove organs from hospital patients. The guidelines are designed to protect potential donors. But critics say they do little to improve safety and fail to address deeply troubling ethical concerns.
Stay up to date with our Up First newsletter, sent every weekday morning.

If you're on social media, there's a good chance you've seen the videos: people getting hot and bothered about the young men Democrats just elected.
"I'm looking at you, Rob Sand. I'm looking at you, Jon Ossoff. I'm looking at you, El-Sayed," said fitness coach Jesse Barton, reacting to the midterm results. "I am looking, I am not the only one, and I'm very happy about what I see."
There are debates over candidates' relative levels of hotness. There are a lot of AI-generated images. And there are many, many montages of the politicians set to sexy pop music.

item.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
item.description:
Elections
Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
November 14, 202612:12 AM ET
From
By
Eric Stone
Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a Democrat, has won the race for governor of Alaska and will replace the outgoing Republican. Here he's seen at a polling station at the University of Alaska Anchorage on Election Day.
Eric Stone/Alaska Public Media
hide caption
toggle caption i
Eric Stone/Alaska Public Media
Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state representative from the small island community of Sitka, won the race for Alaska governor, according to a race call by the Associated Press. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in state history.
Kreiss-Tomkins will replace outgoing Gov. Mike Dunleavy, a term-limited Republican who has been governor since 2018. The state's last Democratic governor was Tony Knowles, who left office in 2002.
Kreiss-Tomkins, known by his initials JKT, made his "high-energy, bipartisan, problem-solving approach" a centerpiece of his campaign.

item.title: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
item.description:

GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
Updated November 13, 20269:34 PM ET
Originally published November 13, 20265:18 PM ET
Hansi Lo Wang
An election worker sorts mail-in ballots at the Miami-Dade County Supervisor of Elections Office in Doral for Florida's primary election in August.
Lynne Sladky/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Lynne Sladky/AP
Voting for this year's midterm elections just concluded, but Republican officials in a number of states are already looking to shape how votes are cast in 2028.
Twelve GOP state attorneys general are pushing to revive the president's bid for mail-in voting restrictions in time for the 2028 election.
On Thursday, they started the process of appealing a September order by U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols, one of the two judges who blocked the U.S. Postal Service from carrying out a plan released in response to an executive order by President Trump.

The nationwide ground stop that paralyzed the U.S. aviation system on Friday has ended, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.
The rare stop, which lasted about four hours, grounded thousands of flights at all U.S. airports in one of the biggest disruptions of the nation's air travel system since the September 11th attacks.
In a Friday night news conference, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that air traffic control facilities had experienced "intermittent" outages of their radar and communications systems beginning earlier in the afternoon. Duffy blamed outdated technology for the failures.
